source.text: Ὡς δὲ ἐκρίθη τοῦ ἀποπλεῖν ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν, παρεδίδουν τόν τε Παῦλον καί τινας ἑτέρους δεσμώτας ἑκατοντάρχῃ ὀνόματι Ἰουλίῳ σπείρης Σεβαστῆς.

records.literal_gloss: When now it was decided the to sail away us to the Italy, they were handing over both the Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion by name Julius of a cohort Augustan.

en.L: Now when it was decided [that] we [should] sail away to Italy, they handed over both Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan cohort.
en.B: Once our voyage to Italy had been decided, they placed Paul and a number of other prisoners in the custody of Julius, a centurion of the Augustan cohort.
en.R: It was decided that we would sail to Italy. So Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius. A centurion was an officer over about a hundred soldiers. Julius belonged to a unit called the Augustan cohort.

fr.L: Et quand il fut décidé que nous partirions par mer pour l’Italie, ils remirent Paul et quelques autres prisonniers à un centurion du nom de Julius, de la cohorte Augusta.
fr.B: Une fois notre départ pour l’Italie décidé, on confia Paul et un certain nombre d’autres prisonniers à la garde de Julius, centurion de la cohorte Augusta.
fr.R: On a décidé que nous partirions en bateau pour l’Italie. Alors Paul et d’autres prisonniers ont été confiés à un centurion qui s’appelait Julius. Un centurion était un officier qui commandait environ cent soldats. Julius faisait partie d’une unité appelée la cohorte Augusta.

es.L: Y cuando se decidió que navegáramos a Italia, entregaron a Pablo y a algunos otros presos a un centurión llamado Julio, de la cohorte Augusta.
es.B: Una vez decidido nuestro viaje por mar a Italia, pusieron a Pablo y a otros presos bajo la custodia de Julio, centurión de la cohorte Augusta.
es.R: Se decidió que viajaríamos en barco a Italia. Entonces entregaron a Pablo y a otros presos a un oficial romano llamado Julio. Tenía a su mando unos cien soldados y pertenecía a una unidad llamada la cohorte Augusta.

sw.L: Na ilipoamuliwa kwamba tusafiri kwa meli kwenda Italia, walimkabidhi Paulo na wafungwa wengine kadhaa kwa akida mmoja jina lake Yulio, wa kikosi cha Augusto.
sw.B: Safari yetu ya kwenda Italia ilipokwisha kuamuliwa, walimweka Paulo pamoja na wafungwa wengine kadhaa chini ya ulinzi wa Yulio, akida wa kikosi cha Augusto.
sw.R: Iliamuliwa kwamba tusafiri kwa meli kwenda Italia. Kwa hiyo Paulo na wafungwa wengine walikabidhiwa kwa akida mmoja aitwaye Yulio. Akida alikuwa afisa aliyeongoza askari wapatao mia moja. Yulio alikuwa wa kikosi kilichoitwa Kikosi cha Augusto.

decisions.choice: we: the narrator includes himself in the voyage
alternatives: the narrator only reports what others told him
decisions.reason: The first person plural, last used in 21:18, returns here and runs through the voyage to Rome (28:16). The narrator says he was on board. The sentence does not say who he is.

decisions.choice: centurion: a Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: Centurions appear often in Acts (10:1, 21:32, 22:25-26, 23:17, 24:23). Julius is answerable for the prisoners (27:42-43).

decisions.choice: the Augustan cohort: a unit bearing the honorary title of the emperor
alternatives: a unit of the emperor's personal guard in Rome
decisions.reason: Augustan was a title of honor given to several units of the Roman army. Inscriptions name a cohort with this title in Syria in the first century, but which unit Julius belonged to cannot be settled.

decisions.choice: they handed over: the officials who held Paul, after Festus's decision (25:12)
decisions.reason: The plural has no stated subject. Festus had decided to send Paul to Caesar (25:12, 25:25); his staff carry it out.

decisions.choice: A centurion was an officer over about a hundred soldiers.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the rank, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R), also where Luke says "we" ("nous prîmes la mer", "nous sommes montés"); speech keeps its own tenses
alternatives: passé composé at every level for the "we" passages
decisions.reason: The voyage is written narrative, told by a companion of Paul in the first person. The passé simple in the first person plural ("nous arrivâmes") is the normal form of a written account and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken today. Paul's speeches on board keep the tenses of speech at every level. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: un centurion at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "un centurion" at Literal and Balanced and follows the English at Readable; here the English Readable keeps "centurion" and explains the rank in a sentence of its own, so French Readable does the same.

decisions.choice: centurión (L, B); un oficial romano, with what he commanded, and then el oficial romano (R)
decisions.reason: The Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers (meaning decision m2). Readable says what he commanded, as the English Readable explains the title, and calls Julius "el oficial romano" through the chapter, the Readable wording for the centurion throughout Acts.

decisions.choice: kikosi cha Augusto
decisions.reason: The unit bore the emperor's honorary title (meaning decision on the Augustan cohort); Swahili keeps the name "Augusto", the form readers know from Luke 2:1, rather than translating it.

source.text: ἐπιβάντες δὲ πλοίῳ Ἀδραμυττηνῷ μέλλοντι πλεῖν εἰς τοὺς κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν τόπους ἀνήχθημεν ὄντος σὺν ἡμῖν Ἀριστάρχου Μακεδόνος Θεσσαλονικέως·

records.literal_gloss: Having boarded then a ship Adramyttian being about to sail to the along the Asia places, we put to sea, being with us Aristarchus a Macedonian of Thessalonica.

en.L: And having boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail to the places along [the coast of] Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
en.B: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was due to call at ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
en.R: We got on a ship from the town of Adramyttium. It was going to stop at ports along the coast of the province of Asia. Aristarchus came with us. He was from Thessalonica in Macedonia.

fr.L: Et, étant montés sur un navire d’Adramytte qui allait naviguer vers les lieux situés le long [de la côte] d’Asie, nous prîmes la mer, Aristarque, un Macédonien de Thessalonique, étant avec nous.
fr.B: Nous montâmes à bord d’un navire d’Adramytte qui devait faire escale dans les ports de la côte d’Asie, et nous prîmes la mer. Aristarque, un Macédonien de Thessalonique, était avec nous.
fr.R: Nous sommes montés sur un bateau qui venait de la ville d’Adramytte. Il allait s’arrêter dans des ports le long de la côte de la province d’Asie. Aristarque est venu avec nous. Il était de Thessalonique, en Macédoine.

es.L: Y embarcando en una nave adramitena que iba a navegar a los lugares de [la costa de] Asia, zarpamos, estando con nosotros Aristarco, macedonio de Tesalónica.
es.B: Subimos a bordo de un barco de Adramitio que iba a hacer escala en los puertos de la costa de Asia, y nos hicimos a la mar. Iba con nosotros Aristarco, un macedonio de Tesalónica.
es.R: Subimos a un barco que venía del pueblo de Adramitio. Iba a parar en varios puertos de la costa de la provincia de Asia. Aristarco vino con nosotros. Él era de Tesalónica, en Macedonia.

sw.L: Na tulipokwisha kupanda meli ya Adramitio iliyokuwa karibu kusafiri kwenda mahali [pa pwani] ya Asia, tukaanza safari baharini, Aristarko, Mmakedonia wa Thesalonike, akiwa pamoja nasi.
sw.B: Tulipanda meli kutoka Adramitio iliyokuwa ikienda kutia nanga katika bandari za pwani ya Asia, tukaanza safari. Aristarko, Mmakedonia kutoka Thesalonike, alikuwa pamoja nasi.
sw.R: Tulipanda meli iliyotoka mji wa Adramitio. Ilikuwa ikienda kusimama katika bandari za pwani ya jimbo la Asia. Aristarko alikuja pamoja nasi. Yeye alitoka Thesalonike katika Makedonia.

decisions.choice: Adramyttium: a port in the northwest of Asia Minor, the ship's home port
decisions.reason: The ship belonged to Adramyttium, on the coast south of Troas, and was working its way home along the coast.

decisions.choice: Asia: the Roman province in the west of Asia Minor
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Acts (2:9, 16:6, 19:10), Asia is the province whose chief city was Ephesus.

decisions.choice: Aristarchus: Paul's companion from Thessalonica
decisions.reason: He was seized in the riot at Ephesus (19:29) and traveled with Paul to Jerusalem (20:4). Paul later calls him his fellow prisoner (Colossians 4:10; Philemon 24).

decisions.choice: ports along the coast
decisions.reason: The places are harbors where a coasting ship would put in.

decisions.choice: nave (L); barco (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the older word "nave" for the ship throughout the voyage, and Balanced and Readable the everyday "barco".

source.text: τῇ τε ἑτέρᾳ κατήχθημεν εἰς Σιδῶνα, φιλανθρώπως τε ὁ Ἰούλιος τῷ Παύλῳ χρησάμενος ἐπέτρεψεν πρὸς τοὺς φίλους πορευθέντι ἐπιμελείας τυχεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: The and next [day] we put in at Sidon, kindly and the Julius the Paul having treated allowed [him], to the friends having gone, care to receive.

en.L: And on the next [day] we put in at Sidon; and Julius, treating Paul kindly, allowed [him] to go to [his] friends [and] receive care.
en.B: The next day we landed at Sidon. Julius was considerate toward Paul and allowed him to go to his friends and be looked after by them.
en.R: The next day we stopped at the city of Sidon. Julius was kind to Paul. He let Paul go to see his friends there, so that they could give him what he needed.

fr.L: Et le jour suivant, nous abordâmes à Sidon ; et Julius, traitant Paul avec humanité, [lui] permit d’aller chez [ses] amis recevoir des soins.
fr.B: Le lendemain, nous débarquâmes à Sidon. Julius se montra bienveillant envers Paul et lui permit d’aller chez ses amis pour qu’ils prennent soin de lui.
fr.R: Le jour suivant, nous nous sommes arrêtés dans la ville de Sidon. Julius a été gentil avec Paul. Il l’a laissé aller voir ses amis de la ville, pour qu’ils lui donnent ce dont il avait besoin.

es.L: Y al [día] siguiente arribamos a Sidón; y Julio, tratando a Pablo con bondad, [le] permitió ir a [sus] amigos [y] recibir atención.
es.B: Al día siguiente llegamos a Sidón. Julio fue considerado con Pablo y le permitió ir a ver a sus amigos para que lo atendieran.
es.R: Al día siguiente paramos en la ciudad de Sidón. Julio fue amable con Pablo. Lo dejó ir a ver a sus amigos de allí, para que le dieran lo que necesitaba.

sw.L: Na siku iliyofuata tukatia nanga Sidoni; na Yulio, akimtendea Paulo kwa wema, alimruhusu aende kwa rafiki [zake] [na] kutunzwa nao.
sw.B: Siku iliyofuata tulifika Sidoni. Yulio alimjali Paulo, akamruhusu aende kwa rafiki zake ili wamhudumie.
sw.R: Siku iliyofuata tulisimama katika mji wa Sidoni. Yulio alikuwa mwema kwa Paulo. Alimruhusu Paulo aende kuwaona rafiki zake huko, ili wampe vitu alivyohitaji.

decisions.choice: Sidon: an old Phoenician port on the coast north of Caesarea
decisions.reason: Sidon lies on the coast of what is now Lebanon, about a day's sail north of Caesarea, where Paul had been held (23:33, 25:4).

decisions.choice: friends: very likely the believers in Sidon
alternatives: personal friends who were not believers
decisions.reason: There were believers in Phoenicia (11:19, 15:3, 21:3-7). Believers call one another friends in 3 John 15, though the word may simply mean Paul's friends.

decisions.choice: care: attention to his needs, such as food and supplies for the voyage
decisions.reason: The word means looking after someone. Prisoners on a journey often depended on friends for their needs.

decisions.choice: be looked after by them
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the care was for in natural English.

source.text: κἀκεῖθεν ἀναχθέντες ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κύπρον διὰ τὸ τοὺς ἀνέμους εἶναι ἐναντίους, τό τε πέλαγος τὸ κατὰ τὴν Κιλικίαν καὶ Παμφυλίαν διαπλεύσαντες κατήλθομεν εἰς Μύρα τῆς Λυκίας.

records.literal_gloss: And from there having put to sea we sailed under the Cyprus because of the the winds to be contrary, \v 5 the and sea the along the Cilicia and Pamphylia having sailed across we came down to Myra of the Lycia.

en.L: And from there, having put to sea, we sailed under [the lee of] Cyprus because the winds were against [us], \v 5 and having sailed across the sea along Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came down to Myra of Lycia.
en.B: Putting out from there, we sailed on the sheltered side of Cyprus, because the winds were against us. \v 5 We crossed the open water off Cilicia and Pamphylia and came to Myra in Lycia.
en.R: From there we sailed on. The wind was blowing against us, so we kept close to the island of Cyprus, where it gave us some shelter. \v 5 We sailed across the sea along the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia. Then we came to the city of Myra in Lycia.

fr.L: Et de là, ayant pris la mer, nous longeâmes Chypre [à l’abri du vent], parce que les vents étaient contraires, \v 5 et, ayant traversé la mer qui longe la Cilicie et la Pamphylie, nous descendîmes à Myra de Lycie.
fr.B: Partis de là, nous longeâmes Chypre du côté abrité, parce que les vents étaient contraires. \v 5 Nous traversâmes la haute mer au large de la Cilicie et de la Pamphylie, et nous arrivâmes à Myra, en Lycie.
fr.R: De là, nous avons continué notre voyage. Le vent soufflait contre nous, alors nous sommes restés près de l’île de Chypre, qui nous protégeait un peu. \v 5 Nous avons traversé la mer le long de la côte de la Cilicie et de la Pamphylie. Puis nous sommes arrivés dans la ville de Myra, en Lycie.

es.L: Y zarpando de allí, navegamos bajo [el abrigo de] Chipre porque los vientos eran contrarios, \v 5 y atravesando el mar [que está] frente a Cilicia y Panfilia, llegamos a Mira de Licia.
es.B: Zarpamos de allí y navegamos por el lado protegido de Chipre, porque los vientos nos eran contrarios. \v 5 Cruzamos el mar abierto frente a Cilicia y Panfilia, y llegamos a Mira, en Licia.
es.R: De allí seguimos navegando. El viento soplaba en contra, así que nos mantuvimos cerca de la isla de Chipre, que nos protegía un poco del viento. \v 5 Cruzamos el mar a lo largo de la costa de Cilicia y Panfilia. Luego llegamos a la ciudad de Mira, en Licia.

sw.L: Na kutoka huko tukaanza safari, tukapita chini ya [upande uliokingwa wa] Kipro kwa sababu upepo ulikuwa kinyume [nasi], \v 5 na tulipokwisha kuvuka bahari iliyo karibu na Kilikia na Pamfilia, tukashuka mpaka Mira ya Likia.
sw.B: Tulipoondoka huko, tulisafiri upande wa Kipro uliokingwa na upepo, kwa sababu upepo ulikuwa kinyume nasi. \v 5 Tukavuka bahari iliyo mbele ya Kilikia na Pamfilia, tukafika Mira katika Likia.
sw.R: Kutoka huko tuliendelea na safari. Upepo ulikuwa ukivuma kinyume nasi, kwa hiyo tulisafiri karibu na kisiwa cha Kipro, ambapo tulipata kinga kidogo. \v 5 Tulivuka bahari kando ya pwani ya Kilikia na Pamfilia. Kisha tukafika mji wa Mira katika Likia.

decisions.choice: sailed under Cyprus: sailed on the side of the island sheltered from the wind
alternatives: sailed below Cyprus on a map
decisions.reason: The sailing term means keeping in the lee of land. With winds from the west, the sheltered side was the east and north, between Cyprus and the mainland.

decisions.choice: contrary winds: the westerly winds of the eastern Mediterranean in summer and early autumn
decisions.reason: Ships sailing west from Syria met head winds, and so worked along the coast of Asia Minor.

decisions.choice: Myra: a port in Lycia, in the southwest of Asia Minor
decisions.reason: Myra was a harbor where ships carrying grain from Egypt to Italy put in, which is why the centurion finds one there (27:6).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: no length of time for the crossing
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts of the Western text add that the crossing took fifteen days. The SBLGNT does not include it. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: kept close to the island of Cyprus, where it gave us some shelter
decisions.reason: Readable explains the sailing term, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: upepo (singular)
decisions.reason: The Greek has "the winds", but the Swahili plural "pepo" is also the word for demons, so the singular "upepo" is used, as the project's Swahili terms settle.

source.text: κἀκεῖ εὑρὼν ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης πλοῖον Ἀλεξανδρῖνον πλέον εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν ἐνεβίβασεν ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτό.

records.literal_gloss: And there having found the centurion a ship Alexandrian sailing to the Italy, he put us into it.

en.L: And there the centurion, having found an Alexandrian ship sailing to Italy, put us on board it.
en.B: At Myra the centurion came across an Alexandrian ship headed for Italy and transferred us to it.
en.R: At Myra the centurion found a ship from Alexandria in Egypt that was sailing to Italy. He put us on that ship.

fr.L: Et là, le centurion, ayant trouvé un navire d’Alexandrie qui faisait voile vers l’Italie, nous y fit monter.
fr.B: À Myra, le centurion trouva un navire d’Alexandrie en partance pour l’Italie et nous fit passer à bord.
fr.R: À Myra, le centurion a trouvé un bateau d’Alexandrie, en Égypte, qui partait pour l’Italie. Il nous a fait monter sur ce bateau.

es.L: Y allí el centurión, encontrando una nave alejandrina que navegaba a Italia, nos embarcó en ella.
es.B: En Mira, el centurión encontró un barco de Alejandría que iba a Italia y nos hizo subir a bordo.
es.R: En Mira, el oficial romano encontró un barco de Alejandría, en Egipto, que iba a Italia. Nos hizo subir a ese barco.

sw.L: Na huko akida, alipokwisha kupata meli ya Aleksandria iliyokuwa ikisafiri kwenda Italia, alitupandisha ndani yake.
sw.B: Huko Mira akida aliikuta meli ya Aleksandria iliyokuwa ikienda Italia, akatuhamishia humo.
sw.R: Huko Mira akida alipata meli kutoka Aleksandria, mji wa Misri, iliyokuwa ikienda Italia. Akatupandisha katika meli hiyo.

decisions.choice: an Alexandrian ship: very likely a grain ship from Egypt
decisions.reason: Egypt sent wheat to Rome by sea, and this ship carries wheat (27:38). Its size suits the 276 people on board (27:37).

decisions.choice: us: the prisoners and Paul's companions, the narrator among them
decisions.reason: The "we" of the voyage continues.

decisions.choice: At Myra; in Egypt (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the place; Readable also says where Alexandria was.

source.text: ἐν ἱκαναῖς δὲ ἡμέραις βραδυπλοοῦντες καὶ μόλις γενόμενοι κατὰ τὴν Κνίδον, μὴ προσεῶντος ἡμᾶς τοῦ ἀνέμου, ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κρήτην κατὰ Σαλμώνην, μόλις τε παραλεγόμενοι αὐτὴν ἤλθομεν εἰς τόπον τινὰ καλούμενον Καλοὺς Λιμένας ᾧ ἐγγὺς ἦν πόλις Λασαία.

records.literal_gloss: In many now days sailing slowly and with difficulty having come off the Cnidus, not permitting us the wind, we sailed under the Crete off Salmone, \v 8 with difficulty and coasting along it we came to a place certain being called Fair Havens, to which near was city Lasea.

en.L: And sailing slowly for many days and with difficulty coming off Cnidus, the wind not permitting us [to go on], we sailed under [the lee of] Crete off Salmone, \v 8 and coasting along it with difficulty we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near which was [the] city [of] Lasea.
en.B: For many days we made slow headway and only with difficulty arrived off Cnidus. Since the wind would not let us hold our course, we sailed in the shelter of Crete, passing Salmone. \v 8 Working our way along the shore with difficulty, we reached a place called Fair Havens, close to the town of Lasea.
en.R: For many days the ship moved slowly. It was hard work to get as far as the town of Cnidus. The wind would not let us keep going that way. So we sailed along the south side of the island of Crete, past the point of land called Salmone. \v 8 We had a hard time sailing along the coast of Crete. At last we came to a place called Fair Havens. It was near the town of Lasea.

fr.L: Et, naviguant lentement pendant bien des jours, et étant arrivés avec peine à la hauteur de Cnide, le vent ne nous laissant pas [avancer], nous longeâmes la Crète [à l’abri du vent], du côté de Salmoné, \v 8 et, la côtoyant avec peine, nous arrivâmes à un endroit appelé Beaux-Ports, près duquel se trouvait la ville de Lasée.
fr.B: Pendant bien des jours, nous avançâmes lentement, et ce n’est qu’avec peine que nous arrivâmes à la hauteur de Cnide. Comme le vent ne nous permettait pas de garder notre cap, nous passâmes à l’abri de la Crète, au large de Salmoné. \v 8 Nous longeâmes la côte avec difficulté et parvînmes à un endroit appelé Beaux-Ports, près de la ville de Lasée.
fr.R: Pendant de nombreux jours, le bateau a avancé lentement. Nous avons eu beaucoup de mal à arriver jusqu’à la ville de Cnide. Le vent ne nous laissait pas continuer dans cette direction. Alors nous avons longé la côte sud de l’île de Crète, en passant devant le cap Salmoné. \v 8 Nous avons eu du mal à suivre la côte de la Crète. Enfin, nous sommes arrivés à un endroit appelé Beaux-Ports. C’était près de la ville de Lasée.

es.L: Y navegando lentamente durante bastantes días, y llegando a duras penas frente a Cnido, no permitiéndonos el viento [seguir], navegamos bajo [el abrigo de] Creta frente a Salmone, \v 8 y costeándola a duras penas, llegamos a un lugar llamado Buenos Puertos, cerca del cual estaba [la] ciudad [de] Lasea.
es.B: Durante muchos días navegamos despacio, y a duras penas llegamos frente a Cnido. Como el viento no nos dejaba seguir el rumbo, navegamos al abrigo de Creta, pasando frente a Salmone. \v 8 Costeando con dificultad, llegamos a un lugar llamado Buenos Puertos, cerca de la ciudad de Lasea.
es.R: Durante muchos días el barco avanzó despacio. Nos costó mucho llegar a la altura de la ciudad de Cnido. El viento no nos dejaba seguir en esa dirección. Así que navegamos por el lado sur de la isla de Creta, pasando el cabo llamado Salmone. \v 8 Nos costó mucho navegar a lo largo de la costa de Creta. Por fin llegamos a un lugar llamado Buenos Puertos. Estaba cerca de la ciudad de Lasea.

sw.L: Na tulipokuwa tukisafiri polepole kwa siku nyingi, na kwa shida kufika karibu na Kinido, upepo usipoturuhusu [kuendelea], tulipita chini ya [upande uliokingwa wa] Krete karibu na Salmone, \v 8 na tukipita kando yake kwa shida tukafika mahali fulani paitwapo Bandari Nzuri, karibu na mji wa Lasea.
sw.B: Kwa siku nyingi tulisafiri polepole, na kwa shida tukafika karibu na Kinido. Kwa kuwa upepo haukuturuhusu kuendelea na njia yetu, tulisafiri upande wa Krete uliokingwa na upepo, tukipita Salmone. \v 8 Tulisafiri kwa shida kando ya pwani, tukafika mahali paitwapo Bandari Nzuri, karibu na mji wa Lasea.
sw.R: Kwa siku nyingi meli ilienda polepole. Ilikuwa kazi ngumu kufika mpaka mji wa Kinido. Upepo haukuturuhusu kuendelea kwa njia ile. Kwa hiyo tulisafiri kando ya upande wa kusini wa kisiwa cha Krete, tukapita rasi iitwayo Salmone. \v 8 Tulipata shida kubwa kusafiri kando ya pwani ya Krete. Mwishowe tukafika mahali paitwapo Bandari Nzuri. Palikuwa karibu na mji wa Lasea.

decisions.choice: the wind did not let them go on: they could not keep their course west from Cnidus
alternatives: the wind did not let them put in at Cnidus
decisions.reason: The phrase has no object. It may mean the wind kept them from going on west, or kept them from reaching the harbor at Cnidus. Either way they turned south to Crete.

decisions.choice: Cnidus: a port at the southwest tip of Asia Minor; Salmone: a cape at the eastern end of Crete
decisions.reason: From Cnidus the ship ran south to Crete and rounded its eastern cape.

decisions.choice: Fair Havens: a small bay on the south coast of Crete, near the town of Lasea
decisions.reason: The name means good harbors. A bay on the south coast of Crete still bears the name. It gave shelter, but was not a good place to winter (27:12).

decisions.choice: along the south side of the island of Crete
decisions.reason: Readable says which side of Crete gave shelter, as the route to Fair Havens shows.

decisions.choice: Cnido, Salmone, Buenos Puertos
decisions.reason: Place names in their usual modern Spanish forms (meaning decisions m2, m3); "Buenos Puertos" translates the name, as the English "Fair Havens" does.

decisions.choice: Bandari Nzuri
decisions.reason: The place name means "Fair Havens", and Swahili translates it as the English does rather than transliterating the Greek.

source.text: Ἱκανοῦ δὲ χρόνου διαγενομένου καὶ ὄντος ἤδη ἐπισφαλοῦς τοῦ πλοὸς διὰ τὸ καὶ τὴν νηστείαν ἤδη παρεληλυθέναι, παρῄνει ὁ Παῦλος λέγων αὐτοῖς· Ἄνδρες, θεωρῶ ὅτι μετὰ ὕβρεως καὶ πολλῆς ζημίας οὐ μόνον τοῦ φορτίου καὶ τοῦ πλοίου ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι τὸν πλοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: Much now time having passed and being already dangerous the voyage because of also the Fast already to have gone by, was advising the Paul \v 10 saying to them, Men, I see that with damage and much loss not only of the cargo and of the ship but also of the lives of us is going to be the voyage.

en.L: And much time having passed, and the voyage being already dangerous because even the Fast had already gone by, Paul advised [them], \v 10 saying to them, "Men, I perceive that the voyage is going to be with damage and much loss, not only of the cargo and of the ship, but also of our lives."
en.B: A great deal of time had gone by, and sailing was now hazardous, since even the Fast was past. So Paul gave them advice. \v 10 "Men," he said, "I can tell that this voyage is heading for harm and heavy loss, not only to the cargo and the ship but to our own lives too."
en.R: We had lost a lot of time. By now it was dangerous to sail, because autumn had come. The Day of Atonement, the Jewish day of fasting, was already past. So Paul warned the men in charge of the ship. \v 10 He said, "Men, I can see that this trip is going to be a disaster. We will lose the cargo and the ship, and our own lives as well."

fr.L: Et beaucoup de temps s’étant écoulé, et la navigation étant déjà dangereuse parce que même le Jeûne était déjà passé, Paul [les] avertissait, \v 10 leur disant : « Hommes, je vois que la navigation va se faire avec dommage et de grandes pertes, non seulement pour la cargaison et pour le navire, mais aussi pour nos vies. »
fr.B: Il s’était écoulé beaucoup de temps, et la navigation était désormais périlleuse, car le Jeûne lui-même était passé. Paul leur donna donc un avertissement : \v 10 « Mes amis, dit-il, je vois que ce voyage va mal tourner et causer de lourdes pertes, non seulement pour la cargaison et le navire, mais aussi pour nos propres vies. »
fr.R: Nous avions perdu beaucoup de temps. Maintenant, naviguer était dangereux, parce que l’automne était arrivé. Le jour du Grand Pardon, le jour où les Juifs jeûnent, était déjà passé. Alors Paul a averti les hommes qui dirigeaient le bateau. \v 10 Il leur a dit : « Mes amis, je vois que ce voyage va être une catastrophe. Nous allons perdre la cargaison et le bateau, et même nos vies. »

es.L: Y habiendo pasado mucho tiempo, y siendo ya peligrosa la navegación porque también el Ayuno ya había pasado, Pablo [les] aconsejaba, \v 10 diciéndoles: «Hombres, veo que la navegación va a ser con daño y mucha pérdida, no solo de la carga y de la nave, sino también de nuestras vidas».
es.B: Había pasado mucho tiempo, y navegar ya era peligroso, porque incluso el Ayuno ya había pasado. Por eso Pablo les dio un consejo: \v 10 «Señores —les dijo—, veo que este viaje va a traer daños y grandes pérdidas, no solo para la carga y el barco, sino también para nuestras propias vidas».
es.R: Habíamos perdido mucho tiempo. Ya era peligroso navegar, porque había llegado el otoño. El Día de la Expiación, el día de ayuno de los judíos, ya había pasado. Así que Pablo advirtió a los que estaban a cargo del barco. \v 10 Les dijo: «Señores, veo que este viaje va a ser un desastre. Perderemos la carga y el barco, y también nuestras propias vidas».

sw.L: Na muda mwingi ulipokwisha kupita, na safari ikiwa tayari ni ya hatari kwa sababu hata ule Mfungo ulikuwa umekwisha kupita, Paulo aliwaonya, \v 10 akiwaambia, "Wanaume, naona kwamba safari hii itakuwa na madhara na hasara kubwa, si ya mzigo na ya meli tu, bali pia ya maisha yetu."
sw.B: Muda mwingi ulikuwa umepita, na sasa kusafiri kulikuwa hatari, kwa kuwa hata ule Mfungo ulikuwa umekwisha kupita. Kwa hiyo Paulo akawashauri, \v 10 akasema, "Enyi wanaume, naona kwamba safari hii inaelekea kwenye madhara na hasara kubwa, si kwa mzigo na meli tu, bali kwa maisha yetu pia."
sw.R: Tulikuwa tumepoteza muda mwingi. Sasa ilikuwa hatari kusafiri, kwa sababu majira ya dhoruba yalikuwa yamefika. Siku ya Upatanisho, siku ya Wayahudi ya kufunga, ilikuwa imekwisha kupita. Kwa hiyo Paulo aliwaonya watu waliosimamia meli. \v 10 Akasema, "Enyi wanaume, naona kwamba safari hii itakuwa msiba mkubwa. Tutapoteza mzigo na meli, na maisha yetu pia."

decisions.choice: the Fast: the Day of Atonement, in late September or early October
decisions.reason: The Day of Atonement was the one fast the law of Moses commanded (Leviticus 16:29-31; 23:27). It fell on the tenth day of the seventh month. The Roman writer Vegetius says sailing was dangerous from mid-September and stopped altogether from mid-November until spring.

decisions.choice: advised: warned them, urged them to change their plan
decisions.reason: The word is used of strong advice. Paul repeats it in 27:22, when the danger has come.

decisions.choice: I perceive: Paul's own judgment of the danger
decisions.reason: Paul does not say God told him. In 27:22-24 an angel brings a new word: the ship will be lost, but no lives. His first warning was the judgment of an experienced traveler (2 Corinthians 11:25).

decisions.choice: Men: an address to the men who decided the voyage
alternatives: an address to men and women
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to the centurion, the pilot and the owner (27:11), all men.

decisions.choice: autumn had come; the Day of Atonement, the Jewish day of fasting
alternatives: the Fast had already gone by
decisions.reason: Readable says what the Fast was and why it mattered, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the men in charge of the ship
decisions.reason: Readable names those Paul spoke to, from 27:11.

decisions.choice: le Jeûne (L, B); le jour du Grand Pardon, le jour où les Juifs jeûnent (R)
decisions.reason: The capital shows that a particular day is meant (m1), as English "the Fast" does. Readable gives the usual French name of the Day of Atonement, "le Grand Pardon", and says what it was, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Hommes (L); Mes amis (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "Hommes !" as an address sounds abrupt; "Messieurs" is too formal for a ship's company in danger. Balanced and Readable use "Mes amis", a friendly but serious way to address a group; Literal keeps the Greek word. The same in 27:21 and 27:25.

decisions.choice: Hombres (L); Señores (B, R)
decisions.reason: Paul addresses the men who decided the voyage (meaning decision m4); "Señores" is the natural Spanish address to a group of men, and Literal keeps the plain word, as Acts 27:21 and 27:25 do.

decisions.choice: el Día de la Expiación, el día de ayuno de los judíos
decisions.reason: As the English Readable: the Fast is the Day of Atonement, in late September or early October (meaning decision m1), the Spanish name being "Día de la Expiación".

decisions.choice: ule Mfungo (L, B); Siku ya Upatanisho, siku ya Wayahudi ya kufunga (R)
decisions.reason: "Saumu" is the everyday word for the Muslim fast of Ramadan; "Mfungo", capitalised, names the Jewish fast of the Day of Atonement (meaning decision) without that association. Readable names the day, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: majira ya dhoruba yalikuwa yamefika (the stormy season had come)
decisions.reason: East African readers do not know an autumn season; the point of the English Readable's "autumn had come" is that the season of storms had begun, and Swahili says that.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἑκατοντάρχης τῷ κυβερνήτῃ καὶ τῷ ναυκλήρῳ μᾶλλον ἐπείθετο ἢ τοῖς ὑπὸ Παύλου λεγομένοις.

records.literal_gloss: The but centurion by the pilot and the ship owner rather was persuaded than by the things by Paul being said.

en.L: But the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and the ship owner rather than by the things said by Paul.
en.B: But the centurion put more trust in the helmsman and the owner of the ship than in what Paul was saying.
en.R: But the centurion did not listen to Paul. Instead he listened to the man who steered the ship and to the ship's owner.

fr.L: Mais le centurion se laissait persuader par le pilote et par le propriétaire du navire plutôt que par ce que disait Paul.
fr.B: Mais le centurion fit davantage confiance au timonier et au propriétaire du navire qu’aux paroles de Paul.
fr.R: Mais le centurion n’a pas écouté Paul. Il a plutôt écouté l’homme qui tenait la barre du bateau et le propriétaire du bateau.

es.L: Pero el centurión se dejaba persuadir más por el piloto y el dueño de la nave que por lo que decía Pablo.
es.B: Pero el centurión confió más en el piloto y en el dueño del barco que en lo que Pablo decía.
es.R: Pero el oficial romano no le hizo caso a Pablo. En cambio, escuchó al hombre que dirigía el barco y al dueño del barco.

sw.L: Lakini akida alishawishiwa zaidi na nahodha na mwenye meli kuliko na mambo yaliyosemwa na Paulo.
sw.B: Lakini akida aliwaamini zaidi nahodha na mwenye meli kuliko maneno ya Paulo.
sw.R: Lakini akida hakumsikiliza Paulo. Badala yake, aliwasikiliza mtu aliyeongoza meli na mwenye meli.

decisions.choice: pilot: the helmsman, the sailing master who steered and navigated
decisions.reason: The word means the one who steers (Revelation 18:17). He was the expert on the sea.

decisions.choice: ship owner: the owner, or the master who commanded the ship for its owners
decisions.reason: The word can mean the owner of a ship or its captain. On a grain ship working for Rome it may be the master under contract.

decisions.choice: the centurion decides: as the senior officer on board
decisions.reason: The centurion's choice settles the matter, though 27:12 says the majority agreed. Why a centurion could decide is not stated; a grain ship serving Rome may have been under his authority.

decisions.choice: helmsman
decisions.reason: In modern English a pilot is someone who guides ships into harbor or flies aircraft. Helmsman says what he did.

source.text: ἀνευθέτου δὲ τοῦ λιμένος ὑπάρχοντος πρὸς παραχειμασίαν οἱ πλείονες ἔθεντο βουλὴν ἀναχθῆναι ἐκεῖθεν, εἴ πως δύναιντο καταντήσαντες εἰς Φοίνικα παραχειμάσαι, λιμένα τῆς Κρήτης βλέποντα κατὰ λίβα καὶ κατὰ χῶρον.

records.literal_gloss: Unsuitable now the harbor being for wintering, the majority made a plan to put to sea from there, if somehow they might be able having reached to Phoenix to winter, a harbor of the Crete looking toward southwest and toward northwest.

en.L: And because the harbor was unsuitable for wintering, the majority made a decision to put to sea from there, if somehow they might be able to reach Phoenix [and] winter [there], a harbor of Crete facing southwest and northwest.
en.B: The harbor was a poor place to spend the winter, so most of them were for putting out to sea again, in the hope of somehow getting to Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix is a harbor in Crete that faces both southwest and northwest.
en.R: The harbor at Fair Havens was not a good place to stay during the winter. So most of the men decided to sail on. They hoped they could reach Phoenix and stay there for the winter. Phoenix was a harbor on Crete that was open to the southwest and the northwest.

fr.L: Et, le port n’étant pas propice pour hiverner, la plupart furent d’avis de prendre la mer de là, pour essayer de parvenir à Phénix [et d’y] passer l’hiver, un port de Crète tourné vers le sud-ouest et vers le nord-ouest.
fr.B: Le port se prêtait mal à un hivernage, aussi la plupart furent-ils d’avis de reprendre la mer, dans l’espoir de gagner Phénix pour y passer l’hiver. Phénix est un port de Crète, ouvert à la fois au sud-ouest et au nord-ouest.
fr.R: À Beaux-Ports, le port n’était pas un bon endroit pour rester pendant l’hiver. Alors la plupart des hommes ont décidé de repartir. Ils espéraient arriver à Phénix et y passer l’hiver. Phénix était un port de la Crète, ouvert vers le sud-ouest et vers le nord-ouest.

es.L: Y como el puerto no era adecuado para invernar, la mayoría tomó la decisión de zarpar de allí, por si de algún modo podían llegar a Fenice [e] invernar [allí], un puerto de Creta que mira hacia el suroeste y hacia el noroeste.
es.B: El puerto no era un buen lugar para pasar el invierno, así que la mayoría fue del parecer de hacerse otra vez a la mar, con la esperanza de llegar de algún modo a Fenice y pasar allí el invierno. Fenice es un puerto de Creta que da al suroeste y al noroeste.
es.R: Buenos Puertos no era un buen lugar para quedarse durante el invierno. Por eso la mayoría de los hombres decidió seguir navegando. Esperaban llegar a Fenice y quedarse allí durante el invierno. Fenice era un puerto de Creta que estaba abierto hacia el suroeste y el noroeste.

sw.L: Na kwa kuwa bandari haikufaa kukaa wakati wa baridi, wengi wao walishauri waondoke huko, ili kama ingewezekana wafike Foinike [na] kukaa huko wakati wa baridi, bandari ya Krete inayoelekea kusini-magharibi na kaskazini-magharibi.
sw.B: Bandari ile haikufaa kukaa majira ya baridi, kwa hiyo wengi wao walitaka kuendelea na safari, wakitumaini kwa namna fulani kufika Foinike ili wakae huko majira ya baridi. Foinike ni bandari ya Krete inayoelekea kusini-magharibi na kaskazini-magharibi.
sw.R: Bandari Nzuri haikufaa kukaa wakati wa majira ya baridi. Kwa hiyo wengi wa watu waliamua kuendelea na safari. Walitumaini kufika Foinike na kukaa huko wakati wa majira ya baridi. Foinike ilikuwa bandari katika Krete iliyokuwa wazi upande wa kusini-magharibi na kaskazini-magharibi.

decisions.choice: Phoenix: a harbor farther west along the south coast of Crete
decisions.reason: The name is the same as the word for Phoenicia, but here it is a port of Crete. Its exact site is disputed.

decisions.choice: facing southwest and northwest: the directions the harbor opens toward
alternatives: facing northeast and southeast, looking down the southwest and northwest winds
decisions.reason: The Greek names two winds, the southwest wind and the northwest wind. "Looking toward" them most likely means the harbor opened in those directions. Some take it to mean it looked the way those winds blow, that is, to the east.

decisions.choice: the majority: most of those consulted, not the centurion alone
alternatives: a vote of everyone on board
decisions.reason: The decision was shared, though the centurion's view carried it (27:11).

decisions.choice: the harbor at Fair Havens
decisions.reason: Readable names the harbor, from 27:8.

source.text: Ὑποπνεύσαντος δὲ νότου δόξαντες τῆς προθέσεως κεκρατηκέναι ἄραντες ἆσσον παρελέγοντο τὴν Κρήτην.

records.literal_gloss: Having blown gently now a south wind, having thought the purpose to have obtained, having lifted [anchor] closer they were coasting along the Crete.

en.L: And a south wind blowing gently, thinking they had obtained [their] purpose, having weighed [anchor], they sailed along Crete close [to shore].
en.B: When a light breeze came up from the south, they thought their plan could be carried out. So they raised anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.
en.R: Then a light wind began to blow from the south. The men thought this was the chance they needed. So they pulled up the anchor and sailed along the coast of Crete, staying close to the land.

fr.L: Et un vent du sud s’étant mis à souffler doucement, pensant avoir atteint [leur] but, ayant levé [l’ancre], ils côtoyaient la Crète de près.
fr.B: Une légère brise du sud se leva, et ils pensèrent pouvoir mener leur projet à bien. Ils levèrent donc l’ancre et longèrent la Crète au plus près de la côte.
fr.R: Ensuite, un petit vent a commencé à souffler du sud. Les hommes ont pensé que c’était l’occasion qu’ils attendaient. Alors ils ont remonté l’ancre et ils ont longé la côte de la Crète, tout près de la terre.

es.L: Y soplando suavemente el viento del sur, pensando que habían logrado [su] propósito, levando [anclas], costeaban Creta muy de cerca.
es.B: Cuando empezó a soplar una brisa suave del sur, pensaron que podrían llevar a cabo su plan. Así que levaron anclas y navegaron a lo largo de Creta, cerca de la costa.
es.R: Entonces empezó a soplar un viento suave del sur. Los hombres pensaron que era la oportunidad que necesitaban. Así que levantaron el ancla y navegaron por la costa de Creta, sin alejarse de tierra.

sw.L: Na upepo wa kusini ulipoanza kuvuma polepole, wakidhani kwamba wamelipata kusudi [lao], waling'oa [nanga], wakasafiri kando ya Krete karibu [na pwani].
sw.B: Upepo mwanana ulipoanza kuvuma kutoka kusini, walidhani kwamba mpango wao ungefanikiwa. Basi waling'oa nanga, wakasafiri kando ya Krete, karibu na pwani.
sw.R: Kisha upepo mwanana ulianza kuvuma kutoka kusini. Watu walidhani kwamba hii ndiyo nafasi waliyoihitaji. Kwa hiyo waling'oa nanga, wakasafiri kando ya pwani ya Krete, wakikaa karibu na nchi kavu.

decisions.choice: having lifted: weighed anchor
decisions.reason: The verb is used without an object as a sailing term for raising the anchor, as in 27:17 of hoisting the boat.

decisions.choice: closer: close in to the shore
decisions.reason: The word is a form meaning nearer. Long ago some took it as the name of a town, Assos, but Assos lies far away in Asia Minor.

decisions.choice: a gentle south wind: a wind that suited a run west along the coast
alternatives: a wind that drove them out to sea
decisions.reason: With the wind from the south, they could follow the south coast of Crete west to Phoenix, about a day's sail.

decisions.choice: raised the anchor
decisions.reason: English needs the object, which the sailing term implies.

source.text: μετ’ οὐ πολὺ δὲ ἔβαλεν κατ’ αὐτῆς ἄνεμος τυφωνικὸς ὁ καλούμενος Εὐρακύλων·

records.literal_gloss: After not much however rushed down from it a wind tempestuous, the being called Euraquilo.

en.L: But not long after, a tempestuous wind, the [one] called Euraquilo, rushed down from it.
en.B: But soon afterward a storm wind called Euraquilo, the northeaster, came rushing down off Crete.
en.R: But soon a very strong wind blew down from the island. It was a storm wind from the northeast, called Euraquilo.

fr.L: Mais peu après, un vent de tempête, celui qu’on appelle Euraquilon, se rua du haut de [l’île].
fr.B: Mais peu après, un vent de tempête appelé Euraquilon, le vent du nord-est, s’abattit des hauteurs de la Crète.
fr.R: Mais bientôt, un vent très fort a soufflé du haut de l’île. C’était un vent de tempête qui venait du nord-est. On l’appelait Euraquilon.

es.L: Pero no mucho después se abatió desde ella un viento huracanado, el llamado Euraquilón.
es.B: Pero poco después bajó con fuerza desde Creta un viento huracanado llamado Euraquilón, el viento del nordeste.
es.R: Pero pronto bajó de la isla un viento muy fuerte. Era un viento de tormenta que venía del nordeste, llamado Euraquilón.

sw.L: Lakini baada ya muda mfupi upepo wa dhoruba, ule uitwao Eurakilo, ukavuma kwa nguvu kutoka huko.
sw.B: Lakini muda mfupi baadaye upepo wa dhoruba uitwao Eurakilo, upepo wa kaskazini-mashariki, ukavuma kwa nguvu kutoka Krete.
sw.R: Lakini muda si mrefu upepo mkali sana ulivuma kutoka kisiwani. Ulikuwa upepo wa dhoruba kutoka kaskazini-mashariki, ulioitwa Eurakilo.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: Euraquilo
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts read Euraquilo, the name of a northeast wind. Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read Euroclydon, a word not otherwise known, perhaps meaning a wind that stirs up waves. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Euraquilo: a wind from the east-northeast
decisions.reason: The name joins the Greek word for the east wind with the Latin name for the north wind, a name sailors would use. Such a wind would drive the ship away from Crete to the southwest.

decisions.choice: from it: down from Crete, off its mountains
decisions.reason: The pronoun is feminine and points back to Crete, not to the ship.

decisions.choice: tempestuous: typhoon-like, a violent, whirling wind
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for a whirlwind or hurricane.

decisions.choice: the name Euraquilo at every level, with northeaster or northeast at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The text gives the wind a name; Balanced and Readable add what the name means.

decisions.choice: Euraquilón
decisions.reason: The wind's name is kept at every level in its Spanish form, with "nordeste" added at Balanced and Readable, as the English does (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Eurakilo, with "upepo wa kaskazini-mashariki" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The wind's name is kept in a Swahili spelling at every level, as the English keeps Euraquilo. "Kaskazi", the Swahili name for the north-east monsoon, would bring in a seasonal wind of the Indian Ocean rather than a storm off Crete.

source.text: συναρπασθέντος δὲ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ μὴ δυναμένου ἀντοφθαλμεῖν τῷ ἀνέμῳ ἐπιδόντες ἐφερόμεθα.

records.literal_gloss: Having been seized then the ship and not being able to face the wind, having given way we were being driven along.

en.L: And the ship being seized [by it] and not able to face the wind, giving way [to it] we were driven along.
en.B: The ship was caught up in it and could not be turned into the wind, so we gave way and drifted before it.
en.R: The storm took hold of the ship. The ship could not turn to face into the wind. So we gave up trying and let the wind carry us along.

fr.L: Et le navire ayant été entraîné et ne pouvant faire face au vent, nous laissant aller, nous étions emportés.
fr.B: Le navire fut pris dans la tourmente sans pouvoir remonter face au vent ; nous nous laissâmes donc aller à la dérive.
fr.R: La tempête s’est emparée du bateau. Le bateau ne pouvait pas se tourner face au vent. Alors nous avons arrêté d’essayer, et nous avons laissé le vent nous emporter.

es.L: Y siendo arrebatada la nave y no pudiendo hacer frente al viento, abandonándo[nos a él], éramos llevados a la deriva.
es.B: El barco quedó atrapado por el viento y no podía ponerse proa al viento, así que nos dejamos llevar y fuimos a la deriva.
es.R: La tormenta se apoderó del barco. El barco no podía girar para ponerse de cara al viento. Así que dejamos de intentarlo y permitimos que el viento nos llevara.

sw.L: Na meli ilipokamatwa [nao] na kushindwa kuukabili upepo, tuliiachilia, tukachukuliwa.
sw.B: Meli ilinaswa na dhoruba hiyo, nayo haikuweza kugeuzwa kuukabili upepo, kwa hiyo tuliiachilia, tukasukumwa nao.
sw.R: Dhoruba iliishika meli. Meli haikuweza kugeuka kuukabili upepo. Kwa hiyo tuliacha kujaribu, tukauacha upepo utupeleke.

decisions.choice: to face the wind: to keep the bow pointed into the wind
decisions.reason: The verb means to look someone in the eye. Of a ship it means heading into the wind.

decisions.choice: giving way: giving the ship up to the wind
decisions.reason: The participle has no object; the ship is left to run before the wind.

decisions.choice: gave up trying
decisions.reason: Readable says what giving way meant for the crew.

source.text: νησίον δέ τι ὑποδραμόντες καλούμενον Καῦδα ἰσχύσαμεν μόλις περικρατεῖς γενέσθαι τῆς σκάφης, ἣν ἄραντες βοηθείαις ἐχρῶντο ὑποζωννύντες τὸ πλοῖον· φοβούμενοί τε μὴ εἰς τὴν Σύρτιν ἐκπέσωσιν, χαλάσαντες τὸ σκεῦος, οὕτως ἐφέροντο.

records.literal_gloss: An island then certain having run under being called Cauda, we were able with difficulty control to gain of the boat, \v 17 which having hoisted, supports they were using, undergirding the ship; fearing and lest into the Syrtis they should fall, having lowered the gear, thus they were being driven along.

en.L: And running under [the lee of] a certain small island called Cauda, we were able with difficulty to get control of the boat. \v 17 Having hoisted it [up], they used supports, undergirding the ship, and fearing that they might run aground on the Syrtis, they lowered the gear, and so were driven along.
en.B: We ran in the lee of a small island called Cauda, and there, with great effort, we managed to secure the ship's boat. \v 17 After hoisting it aboard, the crew used ropes to brace the ship, passing them around the hull. They were afraid of being driven onto the sandbanks of the Syrtis, so they let down the sea anchor and were carried along in that way.
en.R: We passed by the sheltered side of a small island called Cauda. There we were able to pull in the small boat that the ship towed behind it, but it was hard work. \v 17 The sailors lifted the boat up onto the ship. Then they tied ropes around the ship to hold it together. They were afraid that the wind would push the ship onto the sandbanks of the Syrtis, near Africa. So they let out a sea anchor to slow the ship down, and they let the wind carry them along.

fr.L: Et passant à l’abri d’une petite île appelée Cauda, nous pûmes à grand-peine nous rendre maîtres de la chaloupe. \v 17 L’ayant hissée, ils eurent recours à des renforts, ceinturant le navire ; et craignant d’échouer sur la Syrte, ils abaissèrent l’appareil, et ainsi ils étaient emportés.
fr.B: Nous passâmes à l’abri d’une petite île appelée Cauda, et là, à grand-peine, nous parvînmes à nous rendre maîtres de la chaloupe. \v 17 Après l’avoir hissée à bord, l’équipage utilisa des cordages pour renforcer le navire, en les passant autour de la coque. Craignant d’être jetés sur les bancs de sable de la Syrte, ils mirent à l’eau l’ancre flottante et se laissèrent ainsi emporter.
fr.R: Nous sommes passés du côté abrité d’une petite île appelée Cauda. Là, nous avons réussi à remonter la petite barque que le bateau tirait derrière lui, mais c’était très difficile. \v 17 Les marins ont hissé la barque sur le bateau. Ensuite, ils ont attaché des cordes tout autour du bateau pour le tenir solide. Ils avaient peur que le vent pousse le bateau sur les bancs de sable de la Syrte, près de l’Afrique. Alors ils ont jeté une ancre flottante pour ralentir le bateau, et ils se sont laissé emporter par le vent.

es.L: Y corriendo bajo [el abrigo de] una pequeña isla llamada Cauda, a duras penas pudimos hacernos con el bote. \v 17 Y habiéndolo subido, usaban refuerzos, ciñendo la nave; y temiendo encallar en la Sirte, arriando el aparejo, así eran llevados a la deriva.
es.B: Pasamos al abrigo de una pequeña isla llamada Cauda, y allí, con mucho esfuerzo, logramos asegurar el bote del barco. \v 17 Después de subirlo a bordo, los marineros usaron cuerdas para reforzar el barco, pasándolas alrededor del casco. Tenían miedo de ir a dar contra los bancos de arena de la Sirte, así que echaron el ancla flotante y se dejaron llevar de ese modo.
es.R: Pasamos por el lado protegido de una pequeña isla llamada Cauda. Allí pudimos recoger el bote pequeño que el barco llevaba remolcado, pero nos costó mucho. \v 17 Los marineros subieron el bote al barco. Después ataron cuerdas alrededor del barco para mantenerlo firme. Tenían miedo de que el viento empujara el barco contra los bancos de arena de la Sirte, cerca de África. Por eso echaron un ancla flotante para frenar el barco, y dejaron que el viento los llevara.

sw.L: Na tulipopita chini ya [upande uliokingwa wa] kisiwa kidogo kiitwacho Kauda, tuliweza kwa shida kuidhibiti mashua. \v 17 Walipokwisha kuipandisha, walitumia vifaa vya msaada, wakiifunga meli kwa kuizungushia chini yake; na wakiogopa wasije wakakwama katika Sirti, walishusha vifaa, na hivyo wakachukuliwa.
sw.B: Tulipita upande wa kisiwa kidogo kiitwacho Kauda uliokingwa na upepo, na huko, kwa juhudi kubwa, tukafaulu kuidhibiti mashua ya meli. \v 17 Baada ya kuipandisha melini, mabaharia walitumia kamba kuiimarisha meli, wakizipitisha kuzunguka kiunzi chake. Waliogopa kusukumwa mpaka kwenye mafungu ya mchanga ya Sirti, kwa hiyo walishusha nanga ya kuburuta, nao wakachukuliwa na upepo hivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Tulipita upande wa kisiwa kidogo kiitwacho Kauda, ambapo upepo haukuwa mkali sana. Huko tuliweza kuivuta ndani mashua ndogo ambayo meli ilikuwa ikiivuta nyuma yake, lakini ilikuwa kazi ngumu. \v 17 Mabaharia waliipandisha mashua juu ya meli. Kisha wakazungusha kamba kuifunga meli ili isivunjike. Waliogopa kwamba upepo ungeisukuma meli mpaka kwenye mafungu ya mchanga ya Sirti, karibu na Afrika. Kwa hiyo walishusha nanga ya kuburuta ili kupunguza mwendo wa meli, wakauacha upepo uwapeleke.

decisions.choice: Cauda: a small island south of the western part of Crete
decisions.reason: Its lee gave a short time of shelter. Some manuscripts spell the name Clauda; the island is the same.

decisions.choice: the boat: the small boat towed behind the ship
decisions.reason: Ships towed a small boat. In a storm it could fill with water or smash against the hull, so it was hauled aboard. It appears again in 27:30-32.

decisions.choice: supports, undergirding the ship: ropes or cables passed around the hull to hold its timbers together
alternatives: cables run lengthwise from bow to stern
decisions.reason: The words are sailing terms. Ships were strengthened with cables in a storm, but how they were fitted here, under the hull or along it, is not certain.

decisions.choice: the Syrtis: the shallow waters and sandbanks off the coast of Libya
decisions.reason: Sailors feared the Syrtis, on the north coast of Africa. A northeast wind would drive the ship toward it.

decisions.choice: lowered the gear: let out a sea anchor to slow the ship
alternatives: lowered the mainsail or the yard
decisions.reason: The word means equipment. It may be a drag anchor let out to slow the drift, or the lowering of sail. Either way they tried not to be driven too far.

decisions.choice: sea anchor
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the likeliest sense, which the meaning note marks as uncertain.

decisions.choice: that the ship towed behind it; near Africa; to slow the ship down
alternatives: the boat; the Syrtis; lowered the gear
decisions.reason: Readable explains the sailing terms and the place.

decisions.choice: echaron el ancla flotante
decisions.reason: As the English: "lowering the gear" most likely means letting out a sea anchor to slow the ship (meaning decision m5); "ancla flotante" is the Spanish name for it.

decisions.choice: nanga ya kuburuta (a drag anchor)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no settled word for a sea anchor; "nanga ya kuburuta" (an anchor that is dragged) says what it does, slowing the ship (meaning decision). A reviewer who knows the sailors' term may prefer it.

source.text: σφοδρῶς δὲ χειμαζομένων ἡμῶν τῇ ἑξῆς ἐκβολὴν ἐποιοῦντο, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ αὐτόχειρες τὴν σκευὴν τοῦ πλοίου ἔρριψαν.

records.literal_gloss: Violently now being storm-tossed us, on the next [day] a jettison they were making, \v 19 and on the third [day] with own hands the tackle of the ship they threw [out].

en.L: And as we were being violently storm-tossed, on the next [day] they began throwing [cargo] overboard, \v 19 and on the third [day] with their own hands they threw out the tackle of the ship.
en.B: The storm pounded us so fiercely that on the following day they started jettisoning the cargo. \v 19 On the third day they took the ship's spare gear and hurled it into the sea with their own hands.
en.R: The storm hit us very hard. So the next day the sailors began to throw cargo off the ship to make it lighter. \v 19 On the third day they even threw some of the ship's equipment into the sea with their own hands.

fr.L: Et comme nous étions violemment battus par la tempête, le jour suivant ils se mirent à jeter [la cargaison] par-dessus bord, \v 19 et le troisième jour, de leurs propres mains, ils jetèrent l’équipement du navire.
fr.B: La tempête nous secouait si violemment que, le lendemain, ils commencèrent à jeter la cargaison à la mer. \v 19 Le troisième jour, ils lancèrent à la mer, de leurs propres mains, les agrès de rechange du navire.
fr.R: La tempête nous frappait très fort. Alors le jour suivant, les marins ont commencé à jeter la cargaison à la mer, pour alléger le bateau. \v 19 Le troisième jour, ils ont même jeté à la mer une partie de l’équipement du bateau, de leurs propres mains.

es.L: Y siendo nosotros violentamente sacudidos por la tormenta, al [día] siguiente comenzaron a arrojar [la carga], \v 19 y al tercer [día] con sus propias manos arrojaron los aparejos de la nave.
es.B: La tormenta nos azotaba con tanta violencia que al día siguiente empezaron a arrojar la carga al mar. \v 19 Al tercer día tomaron los aparejos de repuesto del barco y los echaron al mar con sus propias manos.
es.R: La tormenta nos golpeaba muy fuerte. Por eso al día siguiente los marineros empezaron a tirar la carga del barco para hacerlo más liviano. \v 19 Al tercer día hasta tiraron al mar parte del equipo del barco con sus propias manos.

sw.L: Na tulipokuwa tukipigwa na dhoruba kwa nguvu, siku iliyofuata wakaanza kutupa [mzigo] baharini, \v 19 na siku ya tatu wakatupa kwa mikono yao wenyewe vifaa vya meli.
sw.B: Dhoruba ilitupiga kwa ukali sana hata siku iliyofuata wakaanza kutupa mzigo baharini. \v 19 Siku ya tatu walichukua vifaa vya akiba vya meli, wakavitupa baharini kwa mikono yao wenyewe.
sw.R: Dhoruba ilitupiga kwa nguvu sana. Kwa hiyo siku iliyofuata mabaharia walianza kutupa mzigo baharini ili kuipunguzia meli uzito. \v 19 Siku ya tatu walitupa hata baadhi ya vifaa vya meli baharini kwa mikono yao wenyewe.

decisions.choice: a jettison: throwing cargo overboard to lighten the ship
decisions.reason: Only part of the cargo went; the wheat was kept until 27:38.

decisions.choice: the tackle: the ship's equipment, such as spars, rigging and spare gear
decisions.reason: The word means equipment in general. What was thrown out is not stated.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "they threw"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "we cast out". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: with their own hands: they did it themselves, in desperation
decisions.reason: The word stresses that the crew had to throw away their own equipment.

decisions.choice: to make it lighter
decisions.reason: Readable says why they threw cargo out.

source.text: μήτε δὲ ἡλίου μήτε ἄστρων ἐπιφαινόντων ἐπὶ πλείονας ἡμέρας, χειμῶνός τε οὐκ ὀλίγου ἐπικειμένου, λοιπὸν περιῃρεῖτο ἐλπὶς πᾶσα τοῦ σῴζεσθαι ἡμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: Neither now sun nor stars appearing for many days, storm and not small pressing on, from then on was being taken away hope all of the being saved us.

en.L: And neither sun nor stars appearing for many days, and no small storm pressing on [us], from then on all hope of our being saved was being taken away.
en.B: Day after day there was no sun and no stars to be seen, and the storm kept bearing down on us with great force. In the end every hope that we would come through alive was slipping away from us.
en.R: For many days we could not see the sun or the stars. The storm kept blowing very hard. Finally we gave up all hope that we would survive.

fr.L: Et ni soleil ni étoiles n’apparaissant pendant plusieurs jours, et une tempête qui n’était pas petite pesant [sur nous], dès lors tout espoir d’être sauvés nous était peu à peu enlevé.
fr.B: Pendant des jours et des jours, on ne vit ni soleil ni étoiles, et la tempête continuait de s’acharner sur nous avec une grande violence. À la fin, tout espoir d’en sortir vivants nous échappait.
fr.R: Pendant de nombreux jours, nous n’avons vu ni le soleil ni les étoiles. La tempête continuait à souffler très fort. Finalement, nous avons perdu tout espoir de survivre.

es.L: Y no apareciendo ni sol ni estrellas por muchos días, y apremiándo[nos] una tempestad no pequeña, finalmente se iba desvaneciendo toda esperanza de que nos salváramos.
es.B: Durante muchos días no se vieron ni el sol ni las estrellas, y la tormenta seguía azotándonos con gran fuerza. Al final se nos iba escapando toda esperanza de salir con vida.
es.R: Durante muchos días no pudimos ver el sol ni las estrellas. La tormenta seguía soplando muy fuerte. Al fin perdimos toda esperanza de sobrevivir.

sw.L: Na jua wala nyota zisipoonekana kwa siku nyingi, na dhoruba isiyo ndogo ikituandama, tangu hapo tumaini lote la sisi kuokolewa likawa likiondolewa.
sw.B: Siku baada ya siku hapakuonekana jua wala nyota, na dhoruba iliendelea kutuandama kwa nguvu nyingi. Mwishowe tumaini lote kwamba tungesalimika lilikuwa likitutoka.
sw.R: Kwa siku nyingi hatukuweza kuona jua wala nyota. Dhoruba iliendelea kuvuma kwa nguvu sana. Mwishowe tulikata tamaa kabisa kwamba tungeokoka.

decisions.choice: no sun or stars: no way to steer or know where they were
decisions.reason: Ancient sailors found their way by the sun and the stars. Without them the crew could not tell their position.

decisions.choice: no small storm: a very great storm
decisions.reason: Luke often says "no small" to mean "great" (12:18, 15:2, 19:23-24).

decisions.choice: being saved: rescued from death at sea
decisions.reason: The verb here is about staying alive, as in 27:31 and 27:43-44.

decisions.choice: was being taken away: hope was slowly lost
decisions.reason: The tense pictures hope giving way little by little.

decisions.choice: survive
decisions.reason: Readable says what being saved meant here, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: Πολλῆς τε ἀσιτίας ὑπαρχούσης τότε σταθεὶς ὁ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἔδει μέν, ὦ ἄνδρες, πειθαρχήσαντάς μοι μὴ ἀνάγεσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς Κρήτης κερδῆσαί τε τὴν ὕβριν ταύτην καὶ τὴν ζημίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Much and going without food being, then having stood the Paul in [the] midst of them said, It was necessary indeed, O men, having obeyed me not to put to sea from the Crete and to gain the damage this and the loss.

en.L: And when there had been long going without food, then Paul, standing in their midst, said, "O men, you should have obeyed me and not have put to sea from Crete, and [so] have been spared this damage and loss.
en.B: No one had eaten for a long time. Then Paul stood up among them and said, "Men, you should have heeded me and stayed in Crete instead of setting out. You would have avoided all this damage and loss.
en.R: The men had not eaten for a long time. Then Paul stood up in front of them and said, "Men, you should have listened to me. You should not have left Crete. Then none of this damage and loss would have happened.

fr.L: Et comme on était resté longtemps sans manger, alors Paul, se tenant debout au milieu d’eux, dit : « Il fallait, ô hommes, m’obéir et ne pas prendre la mer depuis la Crète, et [ainsi] éviter ce dommage et cette perte.
fr.B: Il y avait longtemps que personne n’avait mangé. Alors Paul se leva au milieu d’eux et dit : « Mes amis, vous auriez dû m’écouter et rester en Crète au lieu de partir. Vous auriez évité tous ces dégâts et ces pertes.
fr.R: Les hommes n’avaient pas mangé depuis longtemps. Alors Paul s’est levé devant eux et il a dit : « Mes amis, vous auriez dû m’écouter. Vous n’auriez pas dû quitter la Crète. Alors tous ces dégâts et ces pertes ne seraient pas arrivés.

es.L: Y habiendo [pasado] mucho [tiempo] sin comer, entonces Pablo, poniéndose en pie en medio de ellos, dijo: «Oh hombres, {{plural_you:debieron|debisteis}} haberme obedecido y no zarpar de Creta, y [así] evitar este daño y esta pérdida.
es.B: Hacía mucho tiempo que nadie comía. Entonces Pablo se puso de pie en medio de ellos y dijo: «Señores, {{plural_you:debieron hacerme caso y quedarse|debisteis hacerme caso y quedaros}} en Creta en lugar de zarpar. Así {{plural_you:se habrían ahorrado|os habríais ahorrado}} todo este daño y esta pérdida.
es.R: Los hombres no habían comido en mucho tiempo. Entonces Pablo se puso de pie delante de ellos y dijo: «Señores, {{plural_you:debieron|debisteis}} escucharme. No {{plural_you:debieron|debisteis}} salir de Creta. Así no habría pasado nada de este daño ni de esta pérdida.

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wamekaa muda mrefu bila kula, ndipo Paulo akasimama katikati yao, akasema, "Ee wanaume, mlipaswa kunisikiliza na msiondoke Krete, na hivyo mngejiepusha na madhara haya na hasara hii.
sw.B: Hakuna aliyekuwa amekula kwa muda mrefu. Ndipo Paulo akasimama katikati yao, akasema, "Enyi wanaume, mlipaswa kunisikiliza na kubaki Krete badala ya kuanza safari. Mngeepuka madhara haya yote na hasara hii.
sw.R: Watu walikuwa hawajala kwa muda mrefu. Ndipo Paulo akasimama mbele yao, akasema, "Enyi wanaume, mlipaswa kunisikiliza. Hamkupaswa kuondoka Krete. Hapo madhara haya yote na hasara hii yasingetokea.

decisions.choice: going without food: little or no eating, not a religious fast
decisions.reason: In the storm, fear, seasickness, spoiled food and the work of saving the ship would keep people from eating (27:33).

decisions.choice: to gain this damage and loss: to be spared it
decisions.reason: To gain a loss is a Greek way of saying to escape it, by not running the risk.

decisions.choice: O men: an address to the whole ship's company
alternatives: an address to men and women
decisions.reason: The crew, the soldiers and the prisoners were men. Paul uses the same address in 27:25.

decisions.choice: you should have obeyed me: Paul recalls his warning (27:10)
decisions.reason: He recalls that his first warning came true, so that they will trust what he now says (27:22-26).

decisions.choice: stayed in Crete instead of setting out
alternatives: not put to sea from Crete
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the negative into a natural English phrase.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to the whole ship's company (meaning decision m3), so every second-person plural, pronoun or verb, is the plural_you setting.

source.text: καὶ τὰ νῦν παραινῶ ὑμᾶς εὐθυμεῖν, ἀποβολὴ γὰρ ψυχῆς οὐδεμία ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν πλὴν τοῦ πλοίου·

records.literal_gloss: And the now I urge you to keep up courage, loss for of life none will be from you, except of the ship.

en.L: And now I urge you to take heart, for there will be no loss of life among you, only of the ship.
en.B: Even so, I now urge you to take heart. Not one life among you will be lost; only the ship will go.
en.R: But now I want you to take heart. None of you will die. Only the ship will be destroyed.

fr.L: Et maintenant, je vous exhorte à garder courage, car il n’y aura aucune perte de vie parmi vous, sinon du navire.
fr.B: Mais maintenant, je vous invite à reprendre courage. Aucun de vous ne perdra la vie ; seul le navire sera perdu.
fr.R: Mais maintenant, je vous demande de reprendre courage. Aucun de vous ne va mourir. Seul le bateau va être détruit.

es.L: Y ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} exhorto a tener buen ánimo, porque no habrá ninguna pérdida de vida entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, sino solo de la nave.
es.B: Aun así, ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} pido que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} ánimo. Ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} perderá la vida; solo se perderá el barco.
es.R: Pero ahora quiero que {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} ánimo. Ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} va a morir. Solo el barco quedará destruido.

sw.L: Na sasa nawasihi mjipe moyo, kwa maana hapatakuwa na kupotea kwa maisha ya mtu yeyote kati yenu, ila meli tu.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, sasa nawasihi mjipe moyo. Hakuna hata mmoja wenu atakayepoteza maisha; ni meli tu itakayopotea.
sw.R: Lakini sasa nataka mjipe moyo. Hakuna hata mmoja wenu atakayekufa. Ni meli tu itakayoharibika.

decisions.choice: take heart: be of good courage, stop despairing
decisions.reason: The verb means to be in good spirits. It returns in 27:25 and, as an adjective, in 27:36, when they do take heart.

decisions.choice: no loss of life: every person will survive, though the ship will not
decisions.reason: This corrects Paul's own warning in 27:10, which spoke of loss of lives. The reason follows in 27:23-24.

decisions.choice: None of you will die.
alternatives: there will be no loss of life among you
decisions.reason: Readable says it in plain words.

source.text: παρέστη γάρ μοι ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τοῦ θεοῦ, οὗ εἰμι, ᾧ καὶ λατρεύω, ἄγγελος λέγων· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Παῦλε· Καίσαρί σε δεῖ παραστῆναι, καὶ ἰδοὺ κεχάρισταί σοι ὁ θεὸς πάντας τοὺς πλέοντας μετὰ σοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Stood by for me this the night of the God whose I am, whom also I serve, an angel, \v 24 saying, Not fear, Paul, Caesar you it is necessary to stand before, and behold has granted to you the God all those sailing with you.

en.L: For this night there stood by me an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I also serve, \v 24 saying, 'Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar, and look, God has granted you all those sailing with you.'
en.B: For during this night an angel came and stood beside me, an angel of the God whose I am and whom I worship. \v 24 He told me, 'Paul, do not be afraid. You are to appear before Caesar. And look: God has granted you everyone who is on board with you.'
en.R: Last night an angel from God came and stood next to me. I belong to God, and I worship {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 24 The angel said, 'Do not be afraid, Paul! You must go to Rome and stand before Caesar. And God has been kind to you. God will keep everyone sailing with you alive.'

fr.L: Car cette nuit s’est tenu près de moi un ange du Dieu à qui j’appartiens et que je sers aussi, \v 24 disant : “Ne crains pas, Paul ; il faut que tu comparaisses devant César, et voici, Dieu t’a accordé tous ceux qui naviguent avec toi.”
fr.B: En effet, cette nuit, un ange est venu se tenir à mes côtés, un ange du Dieu à qui j’appartiens et à qui je rends un culte. \v 24 Il m’a dit : “Paul, n’aie pas peur. Tu dois comparaître devant César. Et voici que Dieu t’a donné tous ceux qui sont à bord avec toi.”
fr.R: Cette nuit, un ange de Dieu est venu se tenir près de moi. J’appartiens à Dieu, et je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}adore. \v 24 L’ange m’a dit : “N’aie pas peur, Paul ! Tu dois aller à Rome et comparaître devant César. Et Dieu a été bon pour toi. Dieu va garder en vie tous ceux qui naviguent avec toi.”

es.L: Porque esta noche se presentó junto a mí un ángel del Dios de quien soy y a quien también sirvo, \v 24 diciendo: “No temas, Pablo; es necesario que comparezcas ante el César, y mira, Dios te ha concedido a todos los que navegan contigo”.
es.B: Esta misma noche se me presentó un ángel del Dios a quien pertenezco y a quien adoro. \v 24 Me dijo: “Pablo, no tengas miedo. Tienes que comparecer ante el César. Y mira: Dios te ha concedido la vida de todos los que navegan contigo”.
es.R: Anoche un ángel de Dios vino y se quedó de pie junto a mí. Yo pertenezco a Dios y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} adoro. \v 24 El ángel me dijo: “¡No tengas miedo, Pablo! Tienes que ir a Roma y presentarte ante el César. Dios ha sido bueno contigo. Dios mantendrá con vida a todos los que navegan contigo”.

sw.L: Kwa maana usiku huu malaika wa Mungu, ambaye mimi ni {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na ambaye pia ninamtumikia, alisimama karibu nami, \v 24 akisema, 'Usiogope, Paulo; inakupasa kusimama mbele ya Kaisari, na tazama, Mungu amekupa wote wanaosafiri pamoja nawe.'
sw.B: Kwa maana usiku huu malaika wa Mungu, ambaye mimi ni {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na ambaye ninamwabudu, alikuja akasimama karibu nami. \v 24 Akaniambia, 'Paulo, usiogope. Ni lazima usimame mbele ya Kaisari. Na tazama, Mungu amekupa watu wote wanaosafiri pamoja nawe.'
sw.R: Usiku uliopita malaika kutoka kwa Mungu alikuja, akasimama karibu nami. Mimi ni mali ya Mungu, nami ninamwabudu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}. \v 24 Malaika alisema, 'Usiogope, Paulo! Ni lazima uende Roma na kusimama mbele ya Kaisari. Na Mungu amekuonyesha wema. Mungu atawaweka hai watu wote wanaosafiri pamoja nawe.'

decisions.choice: serve: worship, serve God in devotion
decisions.reason: The verb is used of religious service and worship (24:14, 26:7). Paul tells the pagan crew which God he means.

decisions.choice: Caesar: the Roman emperor, to whom Paul had appealed
decisions.reason: Paul appealed to Caesar in 25:11, and Festus agreed (25:12). The emperor at the time was Nero.

decisions.choice: you must: God's purpose for Paul
decisions.reason: The same word as in 23:11, where the Lord told Paul he must testify in Rome. The storm cannot stop it.

decisions.choice: has granted you: given you as a favor, kept alive for your sake
alternatives: has handed over to your authority
decisions.reason: The verb means to give freely. It may imply that Paul had prayed for those with him, but the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: go to Rome and
decisions.reason: Readable says where Caesar was.

decisions.choice: God has been kind to you. God will keep everyone sailing with you alive.
alternatives: God has granted you all those sailing with you
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the gift into two sentences and says what was given: their lives.

decisions.choice: mira (L, B); left out (R)
decisions.reason: The project's wording for "look" in speech: "mira" at Literal and Balanced, reworded at Readable, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ambaye mimi ni {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}
alternatives: no span, as the English "to whom I belong"
decisions.reason: Swahili says "whose I am" with a free possessive pronoun for God, and free possessives meaning God take the span, as the style guide says, although the English wording has no pronoun to mark here.

source.text: διὸ εὐθυμεῖτε, ἄνδρες· πιστεύω γὰρ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι οὕτως ἔσται καθ’ ὃν τρόπον λελάληταί μοι.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore take heart, men; I believe for the God that thus it will be according to which way it has been told to me.

en.L: Therefore take heart, men, for I believe God that it will be just as it has been told me.
en.B: So take heart, men! I believe God: it will happen just the way I was told.
en.R: So take heart, men! I believe God. Everything will happen just as the angel told me.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, prenez courage, hommes, car je crois Dieu : il en sera comme il m’a été dit.
fr.B: Courage donc, mes amis ! Je crois Dieu : les choses se passeront exactement comme on me l’a dit.
fr.R: Alors, mes amis, reprenez courage ! Je crois Dieu. Tout va se passer exactement comme l’ange me l’a dit.

es.L: Por tanto, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} buen ánimo, hombres, porque creo a Dios que así será, tal como se me ha dicho.
es.B: ¡Así que ánimo, señores! Yo le creo a Dios: todo sucederá exactamente como se me dijo.
es.R: ¡Así que ánimo, señores! Yo le creo a Dios. Todo pasará tal como el ángel me dijo.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo jipeni moyo, wanaume, kwa maana namwamini Mungu kwamba itakuwa vivyo hivyo kama nilivyoambiwa.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo jipeni moyo, enyi wanaume! Namwamini Mungu: itatokea sawasawa na jinsi nilivyoambiwa.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo jipeni moyo, enyi wanaume! Ninamwamini Mungu. Kila kitu kitatokea kama vile malaika aliniambia.

decisions.choice: I believe God: I trust that what God said is true
decisions.reason: With the person in this case the verb means to believe what someone says, as in Romans 4:3.

decisions.choice: men: the whole ship's company, as in 27:21
decisions.reason: The hearers were crew, soldiers and prisoners.

decisions.choice: the angel
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, from 27:23.

decisions.choice: je crois Dieu
decisions.reason: The meaning is trust that what God said is true (m1). French "croire quelqu’un" means to take someone at their word, which is the sense; "croire en Dieu" would say that Paul believes God exists or puts his faith in him in general. The verb "croire" is kept at every level, as the term sheet asks.

source.text: εἰς νῆσον δέ τινα δεῖ ἡμᾶς ἐκπεσεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: On an island however certain it is necessary us to run aground.

en.L: But we must run aground on a certain island."
en.B: But we have to be cast ashore on some island."
en.R: But our ship must be wrecked on an island."

fr.L: Mais il faut que nous échouions sur une certaine île. »
fr.B: Mais nous devons être jetés sur la côte d’une île. »
fr.R: Mais notre bateau doit faire naufrage sur une île. »

es.L: Pero tenemos que encallar en cierta isla».
es.B: Pero tendremos que ir a dar a alguna isla».
es.R: Pero nuestro barco tendrá que naufragar en una isla».

sw.L: Lakini inatupasa kukwama katika kisiwa fulani."
sw.B: Lakini ni lazima tutupwe pwani ya kisiwa fulani."
sw.R: Lakini ni lazima meli yetu ivunjike karibu na kisiwa fulani."

decisions.choice: must: part of what God has said will happen
decisions.reason: The same word as in 27:24: the angel's word includes how they will be saved.

decisions.choice: run aground: be driven ashore
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 27:17 and 27:29, a sailing term for being driven onto land. It came true in 27:41.

decisions.choice: be wrecked
decisions.reason: Readable says what running aground meant for the ship.

source.text: Ὡς δὲ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτη νὺξ ἐγένετο διαφερομένων ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ Ἀδρίᾳ, κατὰ μέσον τῆς νυκτὸς ὑπενόουν οἱ ναῦται προσάγειν τινὰ αὐτοῖς χώραν.

records.literal_gloss: When then fourteenth night came, being driven about us in the Adria, about [the] middle of the night were suspecting the sailors to be drawing near some land to them.

en.L: Now when the fourteenth night had come, as we were being driven about in the Adria, about [the] middle of the night the sailors suspected that some land was drawing near to them.
en.B: It was the fourteenth night, and we were drifting this way and that across the sea of Adria. Around midnight the crew started to suspect that land was coming near.
en.R: On the fourteenth night the storm was still pushing us across the sea between Greece and Italy. About midnight the sailors began to think that the ship was getting close to land.

fr.L: Et quand la quatorzième nuit fut venue, alors que nous étions ballottés sur l’Adria, vers le milieu de la nuit, les matelots soupçonnaient qu’une terre s’approchait d’eux.
fr.B: C’était la quatorzième nuit, et nous dérivions çà et là sur la mer d’Adria. Vers minuit, les marins commencèrent à soupçonner qu’une terre était proche.
fr.R: Pendant la quatorzième nuit, la tempête nous poussait encore sur la mer entre la Grèce et l’Italie. Vers minuit, les marins ont commencé à penser que le bateau s’approchait de la terre.

es.L: Y cuando llegó la decimocuarta noche, siendo llevados nosotros de un lado a otro en el Adria, a eso de la medianoche los marineros sospechaban que se les acercaba alguna tierra.
es.B: Era la decimocuarta noche, y seguíamos a la deriva de un lado a otro por el mar de Adria. Hacia la medianoche, los marineros empezaron a sospechar que se acercaban a tierra.
es.R: En la noche número catorce, la tormenta todavía nos empujaba por el mar que está entre Grecia e Italia. A eso de la medianoche, los marineros empezaron a pensar que el barco se estaba acercando a tierra.

sw.L: Na usiku wa kumi na nne ulipofika, tulipokuwa tukichukuliwa huku na huku katika Adria, karibu na usiku wa manane mabaharia walidhani kwamba wanakaribia nchi fulani.
sw.B: Ilikuwa usiku wa kumi na nne, nasi tulikuwa tukipelekwa huku na huko katika bahari ya Adria. Karibu na usiku wa manane mabaharia walianza kushuku kwamba walikuwa wanakaribia nchi kavu.
sw.R: Usiku wa kumi na nne dhoruba ilikuwa bado ikitusukuma katika bahari kati ya Ugiriki na Italia. Karibu na usiku wa manane mabaharia walianza kufikiri kwamba meli ilikuwa inakaribia nchi kavu.

decisions.choice: the Adria: the open sea between Greece, Italy and Sicily, south of the Adriatic gulf
alternatives: the Adriatic Sea between Italy and the Balkans only
